"outsourcing parental responsibility to lawyers, tech companies, and the government is the last thing Americans should do." But we're already outsourcing it...? Tech companies *already* decide what you and your kids see. Is the argument they should have no content moderation? No algorithm? Just a free-floating sea of whatever shit users dump in?

I truly do not understand this argument from @TheFIREorg. How exactly are parents, who "are in the best position to know what speech their children are capable of handling," supposed to exercise that knowledge when their children are using algorithmic social media?

I am very curious if the people who think "where are the parents?" is the response to the Meta / YouTube lawsuit would also agree that cigarette companies should be free to advertise to children. After all, good parents would never buy their children cigarettes.

I'll also add that if the argument is "good parents keep their kids off of social media" then we're agreeing on the premise that social media is bad for kids, right? And we know that not all parents are good / involved / available parents. So we're just saying, ok, the most vulnerable and neglected kids can be prey for these companies, while the luckier children of engaged parents will escape harm? I dunno, that seems bad.
